newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power prices steady to mixed.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity was mostly steady again Thursday with some changes, most notably in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) region, which moved higher due to talk of a coal unit outage, industry sources said.
On-peak, non-firm next day power for Friday delivery in the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was talked steady to lower in the $14.00-16.00 range from $15.00-16.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.

Line loading problems stifled transmission out of the MAPP region, holding back an abundance of power and keeping prices low, the sources said. Line loading out of MAPP was said to be particularly bad Wednesday, especially through the night when demand usually wanes.
"The line loading in MAPP is a daily interruption, but yesterday it was particularly bad," one Mid-West trader said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was pegged steady at $8.50-9.00 with no takers due to non-existent demand.
On-peak non-firm prices in the MAIN region for Friday delivery were discussed stronger at $17.50-20.50 from $17.00-18.00 on Wednesday.
Traders said a 500 megawatt unit was taken off line in Wisconsin, although the outage was not confirmed.
Off-peak non-firm MAIN power was said to be steady in the $11.00-12.50 range, the sources said.
November MAIN electricity was pegged in the $19.00-19.50 range for delivery of a peak 16-hour block through the five business days of the week.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were talked steady to slightly lower at $17.00-17.50 from $17.00-18.00 on Wednesday.

Prices in the region were unaffected by the outage at American Electric Power's 1,300 megawatt Rockport, Ind. coal fired plant. The plant was taken off line Wednesday and was expected to return to service early next week.
Off peak non-firm ECAR was said to be steady at $12.50-14.50 per MWh range.
November ECAR was said to be discussed relatively steady near $17.40-18.00, with December said to be offered at $19.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak non-firm power for Friday delivery was assessed lower in the $15.75-17.75 range from $16.50-18.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
SPP for the remainder of October was pegged at $17.75-18.40, while November was assessed near $20.50 and December at $20.20-20.40, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
